evals.prompt: Umbraco 17 site (Umbraco.Cms 17.x, ModelsBuilder on, Razor). I want one master layout with the HTML shell, a header partial and a footer partial on every page, and the Article template should be able to inject extra <meta> tags into <head>. Write the files and tell me what I need to click in the backoffice.
evals.expected_output: A layout template with Layout = null, @RenderBody() and an optional @RenderSection for head; an Article child template setting Layout and defining @section; header/footer partials in Views/Partials rendered via PartialAsync or <partial>; backoffice steps using v17 'Master template' wording, template registration and Allowed Templates.
expectations: Every view uses @inherits Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common.Views.UmbracoViewPage (optionally generic); none use Umbraco.Web.Mvc
The layout sets Layout = null and contains @RenderBody()
The layout renders the head section with @RenderSection("<name>", false) (not mandatory) and the Article template defines @section <same name> { ... }
The Article template sets Layout to the layout's .cshtml file name
Header and footer partials are created under Views/Partials and rendered with @await Html.PartialAsync or <partial>, not Html.Partial/RenderPartial
Backoffice steps mention allowing the template on the Document Type (Allowed Templates)
Backoffice steps use v17 wording ('Master template'), not v18's 'Layout template: No layout'
If a real buildable project is available, the build succeeds; if not, the agent does not falsely claim a verified build

evals.prompt: We're on Umbraco 18. How do I make my new 'Landing' template use our existing 'Main' template as its layout from the backoffice, and what does that change in the file?
evals.expected_output: Explains the v18 'Layout template: No layout' button and that it sets Layout = "Main.cshtml" in the child, whose markup replaces @RenderBody().
expectations: Names the v18 backoffice control 'Layout template: No layout' (or 'Layout template')
States the file change is Layout = "Main.cshtml" in the Landing template
Explains the child's markup replaces @RenderBody() in the layout
Uses or links the unversioned (v18) docs URL, not 17.latest

evals.prompt: Umbraco 17 site. Add a site.css with our brand colours (#1b264f, #f5c1bc) and a site.js that logs 'ready', and hook both up so every page loads them.
evals.expected_output: Creates wwwroot/css/site.css and wwwroot/scripts/site.js and references them once in the shared layout.
expectations: The stylesheet is created under wwwroot/css and the script under wwwroot/scripts (or the agent justifies another wwwroot path)
Both are referenced once in the shared layout (<link> in <head>, <script> near </body>), not per template
Served URLs are given as /css/site.css and /scripts/site.js
The agent opened only the stylesheets-javascript reference (and at most templates.md to find the layout), not every reference file
Only the v17 docs link was fetched, not the v18 page
If a real buildable project is available, the build succeeds; if not, the agent does not falsely claim a verified build

evals.prompt: Umbraco 17, ModelsBuilder on. On the Article template render the title (fall back to the parent's title if empty), the rich text body, the article date as dd/MM/yyyy, and the hero image from the 'heroImage' media picker as a 'banner' crop plus an 800px-wide version for mobile.
evals.expected_output: Uses ModelsBuilder/typed values, Fallback.ToAncestors for the title, IHtmlEncodedString or typed body, formatted date, GetCropUrl with 'banner' and width: 800, with null checks.
expectations: Title uses Fallback.ToAncestors (via Value or ValueFor) with the Umbraco.Cms.Core.Models.PublishedContent using
Date is formatted with ToString("dd/MM/yyyy")
Hero image is null-checked before rendering
The crop uses GetCropUrl with the 'banner' alias
The mobile version uses GetCropUrl(width: 800) without a height or crop alias
The img tag has a non-empty alt attribute
If a real buildable project is available, the build succeeds; if not, the agent does not falsely claim a verified build

evals.prompt: I put a new article.cshtml file in the Views folder of my Umbraco 17 site but I can't select it as a template on my Article pages. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains templates are registered in the database; create a template with alias 'article' (Umbraco keeps the existing file), then allow it on the Article Document Type.
expectations: States that a .cshtml file alone is not a template because templates are registered in the database
Says to create a template whose alias matches the file name (article) and that the existing file content is kept
Says to allow the template on the Document Type under Allowed Templates
Mentions Production runtime mode blocks creating templates in the backoffice, or does not suggest doing it on a production site

evals.prompt: I'm new to Umbraco and I need to build a quick demo website for a meeting. Can you create a design with the same header and footer on every page and use our colours (navy and pink)? I don't really know what templates are.
evals.expected_output: Detects the version, explains Template / layout / partial view in plain language, builds a layout, a page template, header/footer partials and a stylesheet in that order, and lists the backoffice steps (register template, allow on Document Type).
expectations: The agent detects the Umbraco version from the project or asks for it before writing version-specific steps
Explains 'template', 'layout/master template' and 'partial view' each in plain language
Creates a layout with @RenderBody(), at least one page template using it, header and footer partials, and a stylesheet under wwwroot/css with the colours
Lists the backoffice steps code can't do: creating/registering the template and allowing it on the Document Type
Opens reference files one at a time as each step starts rather than reading every reference up front
If a real buildable project is available, the build succeeds; if not, the agent does not falsely claim a verified build
